title: TUESDAY SOFTBALL: A day after 18 Ks, Gibson fans 19 in Cavies' win - NewsBreak
text:
By Greg Shashack ,
12 hours ago Carlinville pitcher Hallie Gibson, shown in a game earlier this season at Jerseyville, struck out a career-high 19 batters on Tuesday in a win at Litchfield, one day after fanning 18 in a loss to EA-WR. (Greg Shashack / The Telegraph) Carlinville senior pitcher Hallie Gibson rewrote a record on Monday with a career-high 18 strikeouts in a 4-2 loss to East Alton-Wood River.
Hopefully, the 18 was not written in ink.
Gibson came back Tuesday and struck out 19 in the Cavaliers’ 2-0 shutout of the Litchfield Purple Panthers in a South Central Conference softball game at Litchfield. Carlinville is 5-8 and 1-0 in the SCC. Litchfield is 3-14 and 0-3 in the league.
Lexi Fenton had two hits and Gibbons and Ashlyn Killam drove in runs that came in the second and third innings for the Cavies. But Gibson’s work in the circle ruled the day.
The right-hander signed with Western Illinois struck out the first five batters she faced before Chloe Green’s single accounted for Litchfield’s only hit. Gibson then fanned the next seven in row and 19 of the Panthers’ 21 outs came by strikeout. Gibson, who has 137 strikeouts in 77 innings this season, walked one and worked around one Cavies error.
Gillespie 15, Pana 0 – The Miners scored six runs in the fourth to finish off a four-inning SCC rout of the Panthers in Gillespie. The Miners are 12-4 and 3-0 in the conference. Pana is 6-6 and 1-1 in the SCC.
Paxton Reid pitched a one-hitter for the Miners, while striking out three and walking one. Gillian Smith, coming off a three hit, three RBI game in a 16-2 win over Collinsville on Monday, and Amari Vickery both had two hits and two RBI for Gillespie, which also got two RBI from Laci Schuckenbrock.
Hillsboro 5, Staunton 2 – The Hiltoppers halted a five-game losing streak by defeating the Bulldogs in a SCC game in Hillsboro. The Toppers, who started the season 10-0, move to 11-5 and 1-1 in the league. Staunton is 5-7 and 0-1 in the SCC.
Hillsboro pitcher Ella Schaake threw a two-hitter, giving two runs (one earned) with five strikeouts and two walks. Lainey Weller accounted for both of Staunton’s hits. Grace Burris gave up four runs (one earned) on five hits with two walks and eight strikeouts in 4 2/3 innings to take the loss.
Columbia 6, Roxana 2 – The Shells’ hope of beating Columbia for the first time was lost when then Eagles drew off from a 1-0 lead with five runs in the fourth and finished off a Cahokia Conference win in Columbia. The Eagles are 8-5. Roxana is 11-3.
The Shells, who are 0-13 vs. Columbia since 2000, posted both of their runs in the fifth inning, but were held below five runs for the first time this season. Josie Brannon had two hits for Roxana, which was outhit 12-6. Kassidy Schuyler took the complete-game loss.
Salem 16, East Alton-Wood River 2 – The Wildcats made the trip to Wood River and halted an 11-game losing streak by beating the Oilers in a six-inning Cahokia Conference game at Leroy Emerick Field. Salem is 3-12. EA-WR is 5-8.
The Cats scored in all six innings while rapping out 17 hits and getting aid from seven Oiler errors. Ellie Beachum started for EA-WR and pitched 3 2/3 innings to get the loss. The Oilers finished with three hits.
Belleville East 16, Alton 0 – Five runs in the first inning and nine runs in the second sent the Lancers to a four-inning Southwestern Conference victory over the Redbirds at Rita Menke Field in Belleville. East is 12-6 and 4-1 in the SWC. Alton, whose lose hit came from Izzy Hernandez, is 4-12 and 1-4 in the league.
Edwardsville 16, East St. Louis 0 – Freshman Makaela Pippins pitched a four-inning perfect game to lead the Tigers to a SWC victory over the Flyerettes at East St. Louis.
Pippins set down all 12 batters she faced on 44 pitches, including 33 strikes, with six strikeouts. Brooke Burris hit two home runs and had five RBI to lead the Tigers’ 15-hit offense. Edwardsville pushed its winning streak to nine in a row and its record to 15-9. The Tigers lead the SWC with a 5-0 record.
Carrollton 8, Raymond Lincolnwood 0 – Brookelyn Eilerman retired the last 18 Lancers she faced and fired a one-hitter to lead the Hawks to the nonconference victory in Raymond. Carrollton has won seven of its last eight games to move to 12-6-1. Lincolnwood is 9-6.
Eilerman struck out six and walked one in her shutout. Collins Newton and Courtney Waldheuser both had three hits, Hayden McMurtrie had two hits and Collins joined Kadyn Lake with two RBI for Carrollton.
Concord Triopia 5, Greenfield 4 – The Tigers posed a threat, but the Trojans stayed unbeaten after breaking a 4-4 tie with a run in the fifth to escape with the WIVC win in Palmyra. Triopia is 12-0. Greenfield is 4-5.
Addilyn Tracy struck out 10 and walked one while giving four runs (three earned) on seven in the complete-game win for the Trojans. Mylee Tracy homered and Mia McCombs had two doubles for Triopia.
Greenfield got three hits and two RBI from Tinley Albrecht and two hits from Annabeth Thornton. Jaylynn Pitchford went the distance for the Tigers, allowing five runs (four earned) on seven hits with one walk and no strikeouts.
Metro-East Lutheran 15, Belleville Althoff 2 – The Knights picked up a Gateway Metro Conference victory over the Crusaders at Sigmund Bohnet Field in Edwardsville. MEL is 2-6. Althoff is 0-6.
